page: Google Cloud Platform c4d-standard-8-lssd is a general-purpose server instance belonging to the c4d family. It features 8 vCPUs mapped to 4 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 9B45 processor using x86_64 architecture with multithreading enabled. The instance is configured with 31.0 GB of system memory, providing approximately 3.88 GB of RAM per core. Storage is supported by a single local NVMe SSD with a capacity of 68 GB. No GPUs are included in this configuration, and it does not come with complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Performance benchmarks indicate strong single-core capabilities. The server achieves top-tier results in stress-ng single-core CPU performance, Geekbench single-core scores, and single-threaded compression and decompression tasks using gzip and bzip3. Text processing performance also ranks in the top tier. Conversely, multi-core performance metrics, including stress-ng multi-core, Geekbench multi-core, and Passmark CPU scores, fall into the average tier. Memory bandwidth for both cached and uncached read and write operations remains within average parameters.

There is a clear performance tradeoff between single-core efficiency and multi-core scaling. While text generation for small language models reaches top-tier speeds, prompt processing for medium models is weak, placing in the bottom 25 percent. This hardware profile is qualitatively cost-efficient for workloads that prioritize single-threaded execution speed over massive parallelization. Suitable workloads include general-purpose web serving, database operations, software compilation, and lightweight text processing tasks.

It features 31.0 GB of RAM, offering 3.88 GB per core, and includes a 68 GB local NVMe SSD for high-speed local storage. Benchmark data highlights top-tier single-core CPU performance, single-threaded compression, and text processing. However, multi-core execution, memory bandwidth, and database operations perform at average levels. A notable tradeoff is its weak prompt processing performance for medium-sized language models, though it maintains top-tier text generation speeds for smaller models. This configuration is qualitatively cost-efficient for single-thread-heavy workloads, making it well-suited for general-purpose web serving, software compilation, and light database tasks.
